subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A straight line through (3, 4) forms with the coordinate axes a triangle of area 24 square units lying in the first quadrant. Find the equation of the straight line.

mark_split.label: Use the point on the line

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 22, book p.161. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split rewards the two conditions the question sets, at one and two marks, then the algebra that combines them — two marks for forming and solving the quadratic, which is the only real work here, and two for writing the line and checking both conditions on it. The setting-up line takes one mark because it is one line. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C runs Q19 to Q21 at 8 marks each, answer any 2 of 3, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. AUTHOR NOTE on the number of answers: a line cutting a triangle of GIVEN area from the axes usually gives a quadratic with two roots and two admissible lines. Here the quadratic is (p − 6)² = 0, a perfect square, so exactly ONE line qualifies. That is not a slip: 24 square units is the SMALLEST area a first-quadrant line through (3, 4) can cut off, reached only when (3, 4) is the midpoint of the intercept segment, so the two roots coincide. Dropping the first-quadrant restriction would admit two further lines, x-intercept −6 ± 6√2, whose triangles lie in the second and fourth quadrants; the stem excludes them, and the card says so.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say which two conditions you use, and why there is only one answer here.

steps.label: Set up the intercept form
steps.margin_note: First mark. The question is about intercepts and an area, so start from the intercept form. The triangle lies in the first quadrant, so both intercepts are positive.
lines: Let the line be x/p + y/q = 1
Triangle is in the first quadrant

recall.must_convey: That the line is taken as x/p + y/q = 1 with p > 0 and q > 0.
accept: take the line in intercept form x by p plus y by q equals one
p and q are the two intercepts
the first quadrant means both intercepts are positive
intercept form lo line teesukovali
let the intercepts be p and q, both positive
heard_as: x by p plus y by q

steps.why: The intercept form carries both unknowns the question talks about, so both conditions can be written down straight away without any change of variable.
common_mistakes: Starting from y = mx + c, which hides the intercepts.
Allowing p or q to be negative, which leaves the first quadrant.
steps.memory_tip: The question talks about intercepts and an area, so start from x/p + y/q = 1.

steps.label: Use the point on the line
steps.margin_note: One mark. The line passes through (3, 4), so those coordinates satisfy the intercept form. This is the first of the two conditions.

recall.must_convey: That substituting (3, 4) into the intercept form gives 3/p + 4/q = 1.
accept: put three comma four into the intercept form
three by p plus four by q equals one
the point lies on the line so it satisfies the equation
point ni intercept form lo substitute cheyyali
this is the first condition

steps.why: Two unknowns need two conditions, and this is the one the given point supplies.
common_mistakes: Writing 3p + 4q = 1 by substituting into the wrong form.
Swapping 3 and 4 between the two terms.
steps.memory_tip: Two unknowns need two conditions: the POINT gives the first.

steps.label: Use the area condition
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. The triangle has legs p and q along the axes, so its area is half their product. Setting that to 24 gives the second condition.
lines: Area of the triangle = (1/2) p q

recall.must_convey: That the area of the triangle is (1/2)pq, giving pq = 48 and q = 48/p.
accept: the area is half the product of the intercepts

area half into p into q ani rayali
this is the second condition

steps.why: The two intercepts and the origin form a right-angled triangle whose legs ARE p and q, so the area is half their product with no extra work.
common_mistakes: Writing the area with a modulus and then losing the positive sign.
steps.memory_tip: The legs of the triangle ARE the two intercepts, so area = (1/2)pq.

steps.label: Form and solve the quadratic
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Put (2) into (1), clear the fractions by multiplying by 12p, and the quadratic turns out to be a perfect square — one repeated root, so one line.

recall.must_convey: That substituting and clearing fractions gives (p − 6)² = 0, so p = 6 and q = 8.
accept: substitute q equals forty eight by p and clear the fractions
the quadratic is p squared minus twelve p plus thirty six
it is a perfect square so p is six twice
quadratic perfect square kabatti oke root
p is six and q is eight

steps.why: The repeated root is real, not a slip: 24 square units is the SMALLEST area a first-quadrant line through (3, 4) can cut off, and the smallest area is reached by exactly one line, so the two roots coincide.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 12p but not by every term.
Reporting two different values of p from a perfect square.
steps.memory_tip: A perfect square means ONE line, not none — 24 is the smallest area possible here.

steps.label: Write the line and check
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Put p and q back into the intercept form, clear it, then test both given conditions on the answer — the point and the area.

recall.must_convey: That the line is 4x + 3y − 24 = 0 and both the point and the area check out.
accept: put p and q back to get x by six plus y by eight equals one
the line is four x plus three y minus twenty four equals zero
check the point and the area on the answer

steps.why: Both conditions the question set can be tested on the finished line in one line each, so a slip anywhere above shows up before the answer is boxed.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer in intercept form when a line equation is asked for.
Checking the point but not the area.
steps.memory_tip: Test BOTH given conditions on the finished line: the point and the area.
